1.explanation:
• components/prism-mermaid.js – this is the new file you must create to define the Mermaid grammar (keywords, punctuation, tokens, etc.), following the pattern of every other prism-*.js file in components/.  
• components/index.js – Prism uses this manifest to know which language definitions to load by default; you have to add an import/require for "./prism-mermaid" so it becomes part of the build.  
• dependencies.js – lists language dependencies and load order; even if Mermaid has no dependencies you should add an entry like `"mermaid": []` so the autoloader and build tools recognize it.  
• plugins/autoloader/prism-autoloader.js – the autoloader maps language names and file names; you need to add a mapping for `"mermaid": "components/prism-mermaid"` so that when someone writes ```` ```mermaid ```` the plugin will fetch the right script.  
• components.js – this root file collects all language definitions for the site’s language chooser and documentation; you must include “mermaid” in its array so it appears in the UI.  
• gulpfile/paths.js – the build pipeline glob‐patterns live here; ensure that prism-mermaid.js (and its .min.js) are picked up, or extend the pattern if necessary so the new files get compiled and minified in the release.
1.bug_scenario: A user has added a Mermaid code block to markdown and expected Prism to recognize “mermaid” as a language and apply syntax highlighting, but nothing happens — Prism doesn’t ship a prism-mermaid definition. The sample snippet and the rendered diagram image show a valid Mermaid graph, yet the code block remains unhighlighted because Prism has no Mermaid grammar registered.

2.explanation:
To add Mermaid support you must:  
1. Provide the language definition in components/prism-mermaid.js so Prism knows how to tokenize mermaid syntax.  
2. Update components.js (the master list of languages) so the build system includes prism-mermaid.js in the bundle.  
3. Add an entry for "mermaid" in dependencies.js if it relies on other Prism languages (e.g. markup or JavaScript).  
4. Modify gulpfile.js along with gulpfile/paths.js to pick up the new file in build tasks (concatenation, minification).  
5. Extend gulpfile/docs.js so that the documentation site will generate a page for the new Mermaid language.  
6. Finally, update prism.js if you offer a default bundle that explicitly imports each language—so mermaid ends up in the shipped core script.
2.bug_scenario: Users writing Mermaid diagrams in markdown code fences (```mermaid) get no syntax‐highlighting and Prism does not recognize “mermaid” as a language. The example flowchart shown in the bug report renders correctly as a diagram, but Prism treats the code block as plain text, because there is no prism-mermaid language definition or build configuration to include it.
